newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha higher on firm bids by Japan trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha higher on firm bids by Japan trade.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were higher on Thursday with a Japanese trading house eagerly seeking near-term open-spec cargoes, traders said.
But most other naphtha dealers in the region kept a low profile as market direction remained unclear during the Christmas holidays overseas, they added.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half March was bid at $238.50 a tonne and offers were assessed at around $240.00, compared with quotes at $237.00/238.00 in late trading on Wednesday.
Bids for second-half February were heard at $242.00 against notional offer levels at $243.50.

The backwardation in naphtha's inter-month spreads was barely changed, with first-half February/first-half March talked at plus $6.00/7.00, compared with $6.50/7.00 a week ago. In the low sulphur waxy residue market, trade in January delivery cargoes has been picking up, with levels discussed at about $1.00 over the Pertamina formula, traders said.

Refiner Japan Energy said it was still unclear when it will be able to restart its 110,000 barrel-per-day crude distillation unit at its Mizushima plant. The facility has been closed since a hydrogen gas leak on December 18.
